title: Team wiki where a title stops being a page's identity

initial_repo.README.md:
# wiki

Our team notebook: a folder of plain markdown pages, one file per page, linked
with `[[Page Title]]`. People read and drop files into `pages/` by hand, so
the file format in `wiki/storage.py` is a real interface. See `data/sample/`.

    python3 -m pytest -q
initial_repo.data/sample/pages/home.md:
title: Home
tags: start

Start with [[Onboarding]] and the [[Style Guide]].
initial_repo.data/sample/pages/onboarding.md:
title: Onboarding
tags: people, start

Read the [[Style Guide]], then ask around.
initial_repo.data/sample/pages/style-guide.md:
title: Style Guide
tags: writing

Short sentences. Back to [[Home]].

import pytest

from wiki import backup
from wiki.notebook import Notebook


def test_round_trip_through_a_file(tmp_path):
    nb = Notebook(str(tmp_path / "a"))
    nb.create("Home", "see [[Guide]]", ["start"])
    nb.create("Guide", "text")
    path = str(tmp_path / "b.json")
    backup.save_backup(nb, path)
    copy = backup.restore(str(tmp_path / "copy"), backup.load_backup(path))
    assert copy.titles() == ["Guide", "Home"]
    assert copy.get("Home").tags == ["start"]
    assert copy.target_of("Home", "Guide") == "Guide"


def test_restore_refuses_a_folder_with_pages(tmp_path):
    nb = Notebook(str(tmp_path))
    nb.create("Home")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        backup.restore(str(tmp_path), backup.dump(nb))

import os

import pytest

from wiki.notebook import Notebook, PageExists, PageNotFound

SAMPLE = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", "data", "sample")


def test_create_get_reopen(tmp_path):
    nb = Notebook(str(tmp_path))
    nb.create("Home Page", "hello", ["start"])
    again = Notebook(str(tmp_path))
    assert again.get("home page").body == "hello"
    assert again.get("Home Page").tags == ["start"]


def test_duplicate_refused(tmp_path):
    nb = Notebook(str(tmp_path))
    nb.create("Home")
    with pytest.raises(PageExists):
        nb.create("HOME")


def test_update_and_delete(tmp_path):
    nb = Notebook(str(tmp_path))
    nb.create("Home", "one")
    nb.update("Home", "two")
    assert Notebook(str(tmp_path)).get("Home").body == "two"
    nb.delete("Home")
    with pytest.raises(PageNotFound):
        nb.get("Home")
    assert Notebook(str(tmp_path)).titles() == []

    nb.create("Home", "red fox")

"""The command line the team uses."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys

from . import export, graph
from .notebook import Notebook


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None, out=None) -> int:
    out = out or sys.stdout
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="wiki")
    ap.add_argument("--root", required=True)
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    new = sub.add_parser("new")
    new.add_argument("title")
    new.add_argument("body", nargs="?", default="")
    new.add_argument("--tag", action="append", default=[])
    show = sub.add_parser("show")
    show.add_argument("title")
    find = sub.add_parser("search")
    find.add_argument("query")
    sub.add_parser("check")
    site = sub.add_parser("export")
    site.add_argument("out_dir")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    nb = Notebook(args.root)
    if args.cmd == "new":
        nb.create(args.title, args.body, args.tag)
    elif args.cmd == "show":
        print(nb.get(args.title).body, file=out)
    elif args.cmd == "search":
        for title in nb.search(args.query):
            print(title, file=out)
    elif args.cmd == "check":
        problems = graph.broken_links(nb)
        for title, bad in problems.items():
            print(f"{title}: {', '.join(bad)}", file=out)
        return 1 if problems else 0
    elif args.cmd == "export":
        export.export_html(nb, args.out_dir)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

initial_repo.wiki/links.py:
"""[[Page Title]] links in page bodies."""
from __future__ import annotations

import re

LINK = re.compile(r"\[\[([^\[\]]+)\]\]")


def extract_links(body: str) -> list[str]:
    """Distinct link texts, in the order they first appear."""
    seen, out = set(), []
    for text in LINK.findall(body):
        if text not in seen:
            seen.add(text)
            out.append(text)
    return out

stages.message: Next, people keep asking to rename pages. Add `Notebook.rename(old, new)`. The page keeps its body and tags and its file becomes pages/.md, no old file left behind. `get(old)` then raises PageNotFound, and renaming onto a title that's taken raises PageExists and changes nothing. Here's the catch: other people's pages are theirs, so we must NOT rewrite their text. A page saying `[[Old Name]]` keeps exactly that body, and the link keeps working: `target_of` gives the new title, `graph.backlinks(nb, new)` includes the linker, `graph.backlinks(nb, old)` is `[]`, it isn't in `graph.broken_links` or counted as orphaned, and `stats.most_linked()` (still (title, count) pairs) counts it under the new title. Links written later using a former title reach that page too, through any number of renames. Search goes by the new title (a linker whose body says the old name still matches on its own text, of course). `export.export_html` links to the new file but displays the text as written, e.g. `Old Name`, and writes no file for the old name. All this has to survive `Notebook(root)` being reopened. People also keep dropping .md files into pages/ by hand in the current format (see wiki/storage.py), before and after renames, and existing folders have nothing but those files, so those must keep loading and linking like any other page. You can keep extra data on disk if you need to, but a page's file stays in the current format.

requirements.text: Notebook.rename moves a page to a new title and file, refusing taken titles
Other pages' bodies are not rewritten and their links keep working
backlinks, broken_links, orphans, search and export follow renames
Links written later with a former title reach the renamed page
Renames survive reopening; hand-dropped legacy files still load and link

stages.message:
Rename is great, and now we've hit the problem with it: someone renamed "Alpha" to "Beta" and then made a brand new page called "Alpha". Pages that linked to the original should still mean the original. So titles can come back, and the rule is that a link belongs to the page it was written for:
- When a link is written, it attaches to the page that has that title right then. If no page does, it attaches to the page that most recently had that title. If there's none, it's unresolved (`target_of` gives None) and attaches as soon as a page with that title exists, staying attached if that page is then renamed.
- Once attached it stays attached, whatever happens to titles afterwards. `target_of`, backlinks, broken_links, orphans, most_linked and export all follow this.
- `update` keeps the attachment of any link text still in the new body. A link text that gets removed by an update and comes back in a later one counts as newly written.
- Deleting a page breaks links attached to it and its former titles stop resolving. Those links are unresolved again, same rule as above.
- Links in files from existing folders are written, as far as we can tell, the first time the notebook opens them.
All of it survives reopening, and `backup.dump` / `backup.restore` must carry it too (the dump stays JSON-serializable). Ops has years of old backups with just the pages list, and those must still restore, with links treated like files from existing folders.

requirements.text: A title can be reused; earlier links stay with the original page
Links attach at writing to the current or most recent holder of the title, or when it appears
update keeps attachments of retained link text; removed then re-added links are new
Deleting a page breaks its links and retires its former titles
Attachments survive reopening, including for legacy folders

stages.message:
Last one for now: page history. New `Notebook.history(title)` returns a list of dicts with exactly the keys "rev", "title" and "body", oldest first, rev counting from 1. create, update, rename and revert each add a revision, and a rename's revision has the new title and the same body. History belongs to the page, so it follows renames: `history(old_title)` raises PageNotFound once nothing has that title, and a new page reusing a title starts its own history. A page first seen from an existing file starts at rev 1 with its current body.
New `Notebook.revert(title, rev)` adds a new revision with the body from `rev`. It keeps the current title (and tags), and search reflects the restored body. An unknown rev raises ValueError. The important part: links go back too. Each link in the restored body points where it pointed in that revision, not wherever its text would resolve today. If the page it pointed to has since been deleted, the link is treated as newly written. History and restored links all survive reopening and a `backup.dump` / `backup.restore` round trip.

requirements.text: history lists revisions oldest first, following renames, per page rather than per title
revert restores a revision's body as a new revision, keeping the title
revert restores where links pointed in that revision
History and restored links survive reopening; legacy pages start at rev 1

import json

from wiki import backup
from wiki.notebook import Notebook


def test_backup_carries_history_and_revert_still_restores_links(tmp_path):
    nb = Notebook(str(tmp_path / "nb"))
    nb.create("Alpha")
    nb.create("L", "[[Alpha]]")
    nb.rename("Alpha", "Beta")
    nb.create("Alpha")

import pytest

from wiki.notebook import Notebook, PageNotFound


def test_every_change_is_a_revision_and_history_crosses_renames(tmp_path):
    nb = Notebook(str(tmp_path))
    nb.create("A", "one")
    nb.update("A", "two")
    nb.rename("A", "B")
    assert nb.history("B") == [
        {"rev": 1, "title": "A", "body": "one"},
        {"rev": 2, "title": "A", "body": "two"},
        {"rev": 3, "title": "B", "body": "two"},
    ]
    with pytest.raises(PageNotFound):
        nb.history("A")
    assert Notebook(str(tmp_path)).history("B")[0]["body"] == "one"


def test_a_reused_title_starts_its_own_history(tmp_path):
    nb = Notebook(str(tmp_path))
    nb.create("A", "first")
    nb.rename("A", "B")
    nb.create("A", "second")
    assert [r["body"] for r in nb.history("A")] == ["second"]
    assert len(nb.history("B")) == 2


def test_revert_restores_the_body_as_a_new_revision_keeping_the_title(tmp_path):
    nb = Notebook(str(tmp_path))
    nb.create("A", "red fox")
    nb.update("A", "blue fox")
    nb.rename("A", "B")
    nb.revert("B", 1)
    assert nb.get("B").body == "red fox"
    assert nb.titles() == ["B"]
    assert nb.history("B")[-1] == {"rev": 4, "title": "B", "body": "red fox"}
    assert nb.search("red") == ["B"]
    assert nb.search("blue") == []
    assert Notebook(str(tmp_path)).get("B").body == "red fox"
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        nb.revert("B", 9)


def test_revert_restores_where_the_links_pointed_back_then(tmp_path):
    nb = Notebook(str(tmp_path))
    nb.create("Alpha", "the original")
    nb.create("L", "[[Alpha]]")
    nb.rename("Alpha", "Beta")
    nb.create("Alpha", "the newcomer")
    nb.update("L", "no links")
    nb.update("L", "[[Alpha]] fresh")
    assert nb.target_of("L", "Alpha") == "Alpha"
    nb.revert("L", 1)
    assert nb.target_of("L", "Alpha") == "Beta"
    nb.revert("L", 3)
    assert nb.target_of("L", "Alpha") == "Alpha"
    assert Notebook(str(tmp_path)).target_of("L", "Alpha") == "Alpha"


def test_revert_when_the_old_target_is_gone_binds_like_a_new_link(tmp_path):
    nb = Notebook(str(tmp_path))
    nb.create("Alpha")
    nb.create("L", "[[Alpha]]")
    nb.update("L", "no links")
    nb.delete("Alpha")
    nb.revert("L", 1)
    assert nb.target_of("L", "Alpha") is None
    nb.create("Alpha")
    assert nb.target_of("L", "Alpha") == "Alpha"
